To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have successfully developed the sensor for the transverse field component measurement in the solenoidal magnetic fields and have measured the field in the cooling section prototype solenoid with the required precision.
1) the sensor is capable of measuring field integrals with an accuracy of 10-15% and 2) the field integral over the 20-m cooling solenoid is 0.5-0.7 G-cm.
the transverse field components measured by the compass sensor are consistent with the expected ones, which allows us to use it for the field measurements in the REC cooling section.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the electron cooling technique for the Recycler Ring at Fermilab.
the design and the performance of the magnetic field sensors, the magnetic field quality in the REC solenoids, the design and the fabrication of REC solenoids.
the field measurements on the cooling section prototypes, which are the first step towards the REC commissioning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the field quality of the cooling solenoid is sufficient for the REC project.
the field integral of the transversal field component in the REC cooling section can be maintained within the required limits of 1 G-ccm.
the solenoid field meets the REC requirements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sensor is working properly and the field quality of the cooling section solenois is good.
the sensor is ready to measure the transverse field components in the cooling section.
we have developed a reliable and precise method for measuring the longitudinal magnetic field of the cooling section solenoide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the field quality is sufficient for the REC project.
the field integral is within the design goal of 1 G-ccm for all the solenoid prototypes.
the transverse field components of the REC solenoid prototypes do not meet the requirements for the cooling section.
